title: Find Center of Star Graph
statement: An undirected graph has `n` nodes numbered `1` to `n` and is a star: one node, the center, is joined by an edge to each of the other `n - 1` nodes, and those are the only edges. Each `edges[i] = [u_i, v_i]` is one edge between nodes `u_i` and `v_i`, listed in any order. Return the label of the center node.
constraints: edges form a valid star graph
notes:
## Intuition

Counting each node's degree and picking the one with `n - 1` edges works in O(n). But a star has a stronger property: every edge touches the center, so **any two edges share exactly one node, and it is the center**. Looking at just the first two edges is enough.

## Approach

1. Read the first edge as `[u, v]` and the second as `[x, y]`.
2. The center is one of `u` and `v`. Check whether `u` also appears in the second edge (`uInBoth`).
3. If it does, return `u`; otherwise the shared node must be `v`, so return `v`.

## Example 1, step by step

`edges = [[1,2],[2,3],[4,2]]`.

- First edge: `u = 1`, `v = 2`. Second edge: `x = 2`, `y = 3`.
- `u = 1` equals neither `2` nor `3`, so `uInBoth` is false.
- Return `v = 2`, which indeed touches every edge.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): only two edges are read, no matter how large `n` is.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- The center can sit in either slot of an edge (`[2,1]` or `[1,2]`), so compare `u` with both `x` and `y`.
- Do not assume the center is node `1` or the first number of the first edge.
- When `n = 3` there are only two edges; the method still works because `edges[1]` always exists.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `u`, `v` | endpoints of the first edge |
| `x`, `y` | endpoints of the second edge |
| `uInBoth` | whether `u` also lies on the second edge |

narration.2: Take the two endpoints of the first edge; the center is one of them.
narration.3: Take the endpoints of the second edge; the center is one of these too.
narration.4: Check whether u is shared by the two edges, in either position of the second edge.
narration.5: If u is on both edges, it is the only node they share.
narration.8: Otherwise the shared node, and so the center, must be v.
